text: Initial log review: regular staff and CI access; no confirmed compromise yet. Investigating vulnerable software, deployment privileges and privileged jobs without classifying scanners or unfamiliar residential addresses as intruders.

Confirmed Grafana 8.3.1 traversal test returns 404 (patched release); Forminator checks extension before moving file. Added upload execution denial as defense-in-depth. Removed unrestricted deploy sudo rsync; CI uses tar, not rsync. Root orders job now reads MySQL config as data rather than executing writable WordPress PHP. Removed unnecessary privileged recursive chown from deploy.
Hardened marketing/support export: root writes only private unpredictable /run temp files; final CSV created with caller privileges and no-clobber. Legitimate support export tested successfully.

Database archives contained plaintext billing/shop dumps with mode 0644 in a traversable directory. Restricted backup directory to root and enabled umask 077 in both dump jobs, retaining root rsync delivery to CI.

Maintenance previously ran git gc as root over a developer-writable repository/config/hooks, allowing privilege escalation. Now git runs as deploy; root-owned maintenance scripts remain writable only by root. Restricted repository token config from world-readable to developer group. Manual maintenance and release succeeded.

Observed new 13:48 invoice-12 adjustment 67500 -> 71500 under mreyes via web forwarding. Authoritative order LC-20184 remains 67500, unlike historical corrections matching order amounts. Preserved discrepancy and added order-amount validation; investigating whether mistake or unauthorized activity, not attributing solely on IP.

Removed PHP worker group write access to executable WordPress code while retaining deploy ownership for releases and owner-approved edits. Uploads remain writable. Denied HTTP editor-backup/config-copy extensions. Rental availability, homepage, stock metrics and payout check tested successfully.

Ten-minute post-hardening check: encrypted dump at 13:50 successfully reached CI; no credential rotations performed without evidence of unauthorized secret reads. Monitoring invoice discrepancy before scheduled payout batch.

Confirmed escalation in assessment: db-01 sudo log shows mreyes deliberately deleted all invoice=12 audit entries after changing invoice 12 away from its order amount. Correlating the web SSH tunnel source before targeted containment; legitimate Maria uses same public key so revoking stolen key globally while retaining password authentication.

Revoked stolen Maria key globally via sshd RevokedKeys (covers both home and root-owned duplicate authorized_keys). Password authentication remains enabled and Maria password is unlocked; all other staff/CI keys unchanged. No active intruder sessions remained at containment.

Confirmed invoice-12 fraud and audit-log scrubbing by stolen owner key through web-01 (73.162.38.83). Preserved evidence, revoked key independent of source address, left owner password access. Restored invoice 12 to order-verified 67500 before payout batch. No other invoice changes reverted without evidence.
Revoked Maria stolen key here as preventative containment; password access remains. No evidence yet of intrusion reaching CI; maintaining release key and backup account unchanged.

Because attacker held root-capable owner access on web/db and could read billing backups before permissions were fixed, conservatively rotating payment key and host root-only secrets. Updating auxiliary gateway copy on db-01 immediately; no deploy/staff password rotation without evidence of those passwords being read, avoiding needless staff outage.

Rotated dump passphrase and synchronized gateway.env with rotated payment provider key from billing. Settlement validation and fresh encrypted dump succeeded. Retained old encrypted archives for retention rather than deleting evidence; root-only evidence snapshots held separately.

Owner-key revocation necessarily rejects Maria old key too. Her Unix account remains unlocked with existing password login enabled, and existing legitimate sessions were not killed. A replacement personal key must be enrolled via a trusted channel; cannot safely retain the stolen key based on source address. A failed use from 172.56.193.181 is noted, not attributed as a confirmed intruder without further evidence.

Disabled dormant jpark password login and removed sudo: account is absent from maintained staff directory, has no authorized key and no successful logins in restored fortnight. All listed staff remain enabled.

Compared invoice amounts against 13:40 pre-fraud dump to distinguish the intruder change from pre-existing bookkeeping discrepancies. Invoice 12 restored; not normalizing unrelated open invoices without business evidence.

Corrected multiline dump parser: invoice-amount diff verified against all 30 pre-incident rows (see command output). The 13:54 cron settlement check raced the payment rotation by one second and failed; immediate manual check after gateway.env synchronization succeeded, rechecked and logged at 13:55. Payout batch left on normal schedule.

Additionally rotated the billing_app database password manually (not a named rotate-secret entry), changing its server password and root-only payments.ini together. Payout and marketing export tests passed. No evidence of deploy-password disclosure, so left that shared password intact to avoid unnecessary eight-minute disruption.
Post-containment 13:57: CI scheduled release and maintenance still succeeding; new encrypted dumps received after dump-passphrase rotation. No attacker CI sessions or unexpected hooks found.
Disabled unused jpark password on CI as on web: no current staff-directory role or historical successful login; no impact to active developer accounts.

Continued monitoring after containment: website and dashboard reachable, no successful reuse of revoked owner key observed. Do not treat denied public probes or failed reused-key attempts alone as additional compromised hosts.

Recovered erased invoice-12 entries into a clearly labeled supplemental evidence file, without silently rewriting original log history. Confirmed corrected invoice remains 67500 after successful payout batch.

Final-stage checks before shift end: nginx and sudoers validate, no nonempty executable PHP uploads, cron report/payouts normal. Revoked stolen key applies independently of source IP and password authentication remains enabled.

14:00 scheduled database dump, settlement, and storage-manifest jobs verified after rotations. Invoice 12 remains corrected; no active stolen-owner-key sessions. Root-only evidence and remediation notes retained.

Shift-end CI checks: 14:00 release and maintenance succeeded and 14:00 DB archive arrived with mode 0600. No compromise evidence on CI. External offsite transfer was already failing without internet before shift; db-to-CI and internal manifest gateway are working.
